name: ladspa-sdk
why: LADSPA is a fascinating old plugin standard, but the SDK itself is mostly headers and tooling for developers.

brief.what_it_is: LADSPA (Linux Audio Developer's Simple Plugin API) is a standard for audio processors and effects, the plugins that sit inside audio software. A developer writes an effect such as a reverb, bundles it into a plugin library, and any LADSPA-friendly host application can load and use it. The API is captured in a C header file, and the SDK adds terse documentation, three small command-line hosts (analyseplugin, applyplugin, listplugins), and ten example plugins. The homepage lists hosts such as Ardour, Audacity, LMMS, Rosegarden, Csound and Pd, and many plugin libraries.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a deliberately small compromise: the API aims to be 'a good compromise between functionality, intuition and compatibility but is simple. The "S" in "LADSPA" is meant seriously.' It was proposed on the Linux Audio Developer mailing list and version 1 was finalised on 2 April 2000.
brief.how_it_works: Plugins are compiled into shared libraries that contain one or more individual plugins, each identified by a unique ID. The host discovers libraries by searching the directories in the LADSPA_PATH environment variable (a colon-separated list), or the locations the distribution manages. The API handles only 32-bit floating point data by design, and the host decides how to wire plugins into its own processing, since LADSPA does not impose an architecture. The homepage does not describe the exact function-call sequence; that lives in the header and SDK docs.

brief.install_notes: Many Linux distributions install LADSPA plugin libraries into a central location for you. If a host cannot find your plugins, set the LADSPA_PATH environment variable manually to a colon-separated list of directories. The SDK is a separate download from the homepage and contains the docs, hosts and example plugins. The homepage shows no build commands, and the README-style commands for building the SDK were not on the page I read.
brief.standout: It is a tiny, deliberately minimal plugin API from 2000 that still underpins a large ecosystem of Linux audio plugins and hosts. Its authors chose to leave out features like non-float data types on purpose, which is unusual for a plugin standard.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage gives no current version number beyond 1.1, no last release date, and no last-commit information. Its history section is dated (version 1 in April 2000). I did not follow the SDK download link to check for newer releases.
brief.caveats: The homepage only supports 32-bit float data, by design. It is LGPL-licensed, and the author says LGPL is not intended as the final license and that commercial use may be unclear. The page says LADSPA has been used on other platforms but those are not supported on this website. The SDK is described as mostly developer material (headers, docs, and small example hosts and plugins), not an end-user tool. The site gives no commands with flags or usage, so the hosts are only named. Unclear whether the SDK builds cleanly on modern systems.
quotes: LADSPA is a standard that allows software audio processors and effects to be plugged into a wide range of audio synthesis and recording packages.
Plugin writers can start from example plugins or just the API and code up new plugins very quickly.
